questions.stem: Social media has become a ubiquitous force in our daily lives. In addition to keeping in touch with friends, or simply browsing through their status updates, people have the whole world at their fingertips. However, many people may only see the best, constructed versions of others, and not the whole story. People, therefore, may feel isolated when they compare their lives with the seemingly perfect lives of others. For those who depend on social media for validation, they may end up feeling empty themselves. According to the passage, what is true about social media?

options.A: People see the worst versions of others.
options.B: It is best used for browsing celebrity gossip.
options.C: People can become storytellers through it.
options.D: It can make people feel lonely.

questions.explain:
社交媒體已成為我們日常生活中無處不在的力量。 除了與朋友保持聯繫，或
者只是瀏覽他們的狀態更新之外，人們還可以觸手可及整個世界。 然而，許
多人可能只看到其他人最好的、構建的版本，而不是整個故事。 因此，當人
們將自己的生活與他人看似完美的生活進行比較時，他們可能會感到孤立。
對於那些依賴社交媒體進行驗證的人來說，他們最終可能會感到空虛。 根據
這篇文章，社交媒體的真䋿情況是什麼？ 依照上下文答案為d (它會讓人們感
到孤獨)

questions.stem: Modern malware is sneaky. Different kinds of malware can do anything from tracking keystrokes hoping to get useful information to stealing just a little bit of ad revenue or system resources. Back in the 1990s, however, computer viruses were not nearly as sophisticated. If today's malware were a criminal, it would be a con artist or even a gentleman thief. Early viruses were more like vandals breaking windows with rocks. How does the author develop the passage?

options.C: By asking readers a question first.
options.D: By using the cause and effect mode.

questions.explain:
現代惡意軟件是偷偷摸摸的。 不同種類的惡意軟件可以做任何事情，從跟踪
希望獲得有用信息的擊鍵到竊取一點點廣告收入或系統資源。 然而，回到
1990 年代，計算機病毒並沒有那麼複雜。 如果今天的惡意軟件是罪犯，那它
就是騙子，甚至是紳士小偷。 早期的病毒更像是用石頭打破窗戶的破壞者。
作者是如何發展段落的? 依照上下文答案為b (通過比較和對比)

questions.stem: American football is a dangerous game. It is a full-contact sport, so it is common for players to twist joints, break bones, bleed internally, and hit their heads. Doctors have begun to think that the sport is just too dangerous, especially in regard to head injuries. In a recent study, 165 people who had played football at the high school, college, or professional level donated their brains to science after they died. Of these people, nearly 80 percent showed signs of long-term brain damage. Which type of football injury worries doctors the most?
questions.explain:
